message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | LA Time Zone | Berlin Time Zone | Difference | Berlin is ___ hours ahead |
|--------|--------------|------------------|------------|---------------------------|
| **Standard time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | +9 h | 9 |
| **Daylight‑saving time** (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | +9 h | 9 |
| **Overlap period 1** (US DST starts earlier) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | +8 h | 8 |
| **Overlap period 2** (EU DST ends earlier) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | +10 h | 10 |

### Why the overlap periods exist
- **US DST** starts on the **second Sunday in March** and ends on the **first Sunday in November**.  
- **EU DST** starts on the **last Sunday in March** and ends on the **last Sunday in October**.

Because the start and end dates differ by a few weeks, there are short windows where the two regions are on different DST schedules:

| Year | Overlap 1 (US ahead) | Overlap 2 (EU ahead) |
|------|----------------------|----------------------|
| 2024 | Mar 10 – Mar 31 | Oct 27 – Nov 3 |
| 2025 | Mar 9 – Mar 30 | Oct 26 – Nov 2 |
| 2026 | Mar 8 – Mar 29 | Oct 25 – Nov 1 |

### Current situation (2026‑10‑16)
- **Los Angeles**: on DST (UTC‑7)  
- **Berlin**: on DST (UTC+2)  
- **Difference**: **9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead).

---

#### Quick reference
- **Typical difference**: **9 hours** (Berlin ahead).  
- **When LA is on DST but Berlin is still on standard time** (early March): **8 hours**.  
- **When Berlin has ended DST but LA is still on DST** (late October): **10 hours**.

Feel free to ask if you need the exact offset for a specific date!
